Abstract
This report summarizes the contents of study PRJEB1234 as retrieved from the European Nucleotide Archive (ENA) via the BRC ENA study lookup. I queried the ENA filereport for accession PRJEB1234 (function call: brc_ena_study with study_accession = "PRJEB1234"). The ENA response reports a study titled "A haplotype map of foxtail millet genome", first public 2013-06-06, with a total run_count = 916 and organisms_in_runs listing two species (Setaria italica, Setaria viridis). Because the API response exceeded a server size cap, the service returned a trimmed sample of 28 run records (size_capped.returned = 28) with detailed per-run fields (run accession, sample accession, library strategy/layout, read/base counts, instrument, and paired FASTQ HTTPS URLs). All 28 returned records have scientific_name = "Setaria italica" and library_strategy = "WGS"; each returned run includes paired-end FASTQ HTTPS links (example: https://ftp.sra.ebi.ac.uk/vol1/fastq/ERR214/ERR214765/ERR214765_1.fastq.gz). These results matter because they identify (1) the study metadata and scope (916 whole-genome sequencing runs across two Setaria species) and (2) how to page or fetch the full run list (the response was truncated; the full set requires pagination or targeted run requests).

I. Introduction
Background. PRJEB1234 is an ENA study accession. ENA stores sequencing study metadata and provides FTP/HTTP links to raw sequencing files (FASTQ). Knowing a study’s run count, organisms, and available FASTQ links is necessary for reanalysis, sequence download, and planning downstream bioinformatic workflows.

Literature Review. No literature was retrieved for this query.

Knowledge Gap. Before querying ENA, the exact run count, the organisms represented, per-run file locations, and the study’s first-public date were unknown.

Objective & Hypothesis. Objective: to retrieve the ENA metadata for PRJEB1234 and report the study title, first-public date, total run count, organisms present, and example per-run FASTQ links. Hypothesis: the ENA filereport will provide study-level metadata and a list of run records including FTP/HTTPS FASTQ links.

II. Materials and Methods
Study Design. A single targeted API query to ENA’s filereport endpoint (wrapped by the BRC tool brc_ena_study) was used to obtain study-level metadata and a sample of run records. This direct approach returns both study metadata and run-level fields suitable for assessing data availability.

Materials. The database queried:
- European Nucleotide Archive (ENA) via the brc_ena_study tool (functions.brc_ena_study).

Procedures. Tool calls (exact):
1) brc_ena_study with parameters:
   - study_accession: "PRJEB1234"
   This is the only tool call made in this session, returning the JSON shown in the provenance.

The ENA tool returned:
- study.study_title
- study.first_public
- run_count
- organisms_in_runs (array)
- results (array of run records; trimmed to 28 in this response)
- api_call.url and api_call.params
- size_capped block with trimming metadata

Statistical Analysis. Numbers reported come directly from the JSON fields:
- Total runs (run_count) = value of response["run_count"] (denominator for “total runs”).
- Total matching (size_capped.total_matching) = response["size_capped"]["total_matching"] when provided.
- Returned records count = length(response["results"]) = response["size_capped"]["returned"] when trim applied (numerator for the sample shown).
- Organism count = length(response["organisms_in_runs"]) derived from the array element count.
- Per-run attributes (library_strategy, layout, read_count, base_count) were read directly from each returned result object; no aggregation beyond counts and simple proportions was performed. No deduplication was needed because run_accession is unique in the returned sample.

III. Results
Table 1 summarizes the key study-level metadata and the API pagination/trimming status.

Table 1. Study-level metadata and API return summary
| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Study accession | PRJEB1234 |
| Secondary study accession | ERP002070 |
| Study title | A haplotype map of foxtail millet genome |
| First public date | 2013-06-06 |
| Total runs reported by API (run_count) | 916 |
| Total matching runs (size_capped.total_matching) | 916 |
| Number of organisms_in_runs | 2 |
| Organisms listed in study-level summary | Setaria italica; Setaria viridis |
| Number of run records returned in this response (trimmed sample) | 28 |
| Instrument platform (example from returned records) | ILLUMINA (Illumina Genome Analyzer) |
| Library strategy (returned sample) | WGS (all returned records) |
| Read layout in returned sample | PAIRED (all returned records) |
| Example FASTQ HTTPS URL (first returned run) | https://ftp.sra.ebi.ac.uk/vol1/fastq/ERR214/ERR214765/ERR214765_1.fastq.gz |

Findings.
- The ENA filereport lists run_count = 916 for PRJEB1234.
- The study-level organisms_in_runs array contains 2 unique scientific names: "Setaria italica" and "Setaria viridis".
- The API response was trimmed; the response includes a size_capped block stating total_matching = 916 and returned = 28. Thus 28 run records are included in this API output as a sample; these 28 are not the complete set of 916 runs.
- In the 28 returned run records, every result entry has scientific_name = "Setaria italica" and library_strategy = "WGS".
- Each returned run record contains paired FASTQ HTTPS links (example: https://ftp.sra.ebi.ac.uk/vol1/fastq/ERR214/ERR214765/ERR214765_1.fastq.gz and the corresponding _2.gz).

IV. Discussion
Interpretation. The query successfully retrieved study metadata for PRJEB1234 and a trimmed sample of run records. The study is titled "A haplotype map of foxtail millet genome" and was first made public on 2013-06-06. ENA reports 916 sequencing runs associated with this study; the returned JSON was truncated by the server and included a 28-record sample. The sample shows WGS paired-end Illumina runs for Setaria italica; at least one other species (Setaria viridis) appears in the project-level organisms list but was not present among the 28 records shown in the trimmed sample.

Context. The returned data fields (run accessions, sample accessions, read/base counts, library metadata, instrument model, and FASTQ HTTPS links) match the ENA filereport output convention and provide the information necessary to download raw data or to page the full run list. The api_call.url in the response pinpoints the ENA filereport endpoint used.

Limitations.
- The ENA response was size-capped and trimmed: the server explicitly states the full result contains 916 matching runs but returned only 28 records in this payload. Therefore the per-run sample is not exhaustive and cannot be used to infer the distribution of organisms, instruments, or library strategies across all 916 runs.
- The "organisms_in_runs" array indicates the study contains more than one organism; because the returned sample includes only Setaria italica, the distribution between S. italica and S. viridis across all runs is unknown from this trimmed response.
- Collection_date fields in the returned sample are empty, so geographic/temporal provenance of individual samples is not available from the sample shown.
- The provenance provided is the ENA filereport endpoint and specific per-run FASTQ links; the study submitter metadata (authors, publication) was not retrieved beyond the study title and first_public date.

Conclusion & Future Directions. The ENA holds 916 runs for PRJEB1234 (study title: "A haplotype map of foxtail millet genome", first public 2013-06-06). To obtain the complete run list or to download raw FASTQ files, request paginated run results or query specific run accessions. Recommended next queries:
- Use brc_ena_runs (or brc_ena_study with pagination parameters, or brc_ena_runs tooling) to page through runs (specify offset and limit) until all 916 runs are retrieved.
- Request metadata for a specific run accession (e.g., ERR214765) to fetch full per-run details or to download FASTQ files.
- If sample collection dates or locations are needed, fetch sample-level metadata for the sample_accession values (SAMEA...).

References
[1] ENA filereport API (provenance from tool result): https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ena/portal/api/filereport
[2] Example FASTQ HTTPS URL returned in the response (first run in returned sample): https://ftp.sra.ebi.ac.uk/vol1/fastq/ERR214/ERR214765/ERR214765_1.fastq.gz

Acknowledgments
Data provided by the European Nucleotide Archive (ENA) / EMBL-EBI as returned by the brc_ena_study query for PRJEB1234.
